touches.text: Instance: every device has at least one; a singleton is instance 0.
HARD BOUNDARY: everything about a device is encapsulated in itself.
An internal device is its own process. An external device depends on what it wraps (5.8.3.7).
Devices are peers with different jobs. The operator is one of them (7).
A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.
A device owns its state: only the device writes under its own ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ tree.
Database: because faster (11.3.4).
On every Windows box, what Cairn starts runs without a console window by default; a window opens only when someone asks for one. WHY: the boxes serve him (the media box showed pop-ups during videos).

One bus per cairn instance, not per host. Each box runs its own bus, and the buses talk to one another, so a device always talks to the bus on its own box; together they are the instance's one bus. A device runs on one box; the other boxes reach it over the buses. No box needs a full set of devices. WHY: so the instance can run several heavy tasks at once across boxes.

Every box runs all the foundational things: a bus, a ground loop, the shims. They are the Cairn device's machines, and there is only one Cairn device: a singleton within the swarm, owning them on every box. WHY: Cairn is the system in aggregate, which is not the same thing as the host (6.6); a box is part of the host, and the swarm of boxes is still one Cairn.
DATABASE PROXY DEVICE (cairn/devices/dbproxy/)
The only way to the database. WHY: the authentication is wrapped up in it, and every table has exactly one owner who gates every write; an ownerless table can't be made (Postgres refuses it).
Device name on the command line and bus: database (eg cairn database show).
Its main customer is the librarian, which owns the graph trees; other devices reach the trees through the librarian's commands, not the database proxy, which keeps its bus traffic small.
Publishes a client tool (connect, read, write, query ...) that talks to the database over its socket, no bus hop: faster (2.3.7.1.1).
Postgres itself is a host service, installed and upgraded by Recovery (6.3.5); Rescue when it won't start.

A remote box keeps its own database and syncs it with the home box's (6.3.7.4). Node rows are the same on every box; the sync fills the blanks a box holds open (4.3.1.5.1.1). WHY: the local copy is fast, and the sync is the backup.

Direction: home to remote. Every write goes to the home, so no node is held only by a remote; a box fills from the home, or from another host's proxy, but every row was written at the home (4.3.1.5.1.4.1.2). - akienasus_cc_0

Who holds tables: every table of learning is a tree in the memory model (4.3.1.5), owned by the librarian and delegated to the devices that learn. A table that is not learning is an exception and names why; the bus's message table is the first (5.5.3.4.1).

Every box runs its own instance of the database proxy, and everything on that box talks only to it (4.3.1.5.1.4.1.1). Each box's proxy is its own instance (1.3.4), so this agrees with 5.5.3.8 ("a device runs on one box"): no instance is duplicated, the class has one instance per box, like the foundational set of 5.5.3.8.1. WHY: the local read is fast, and the cache it fills is every box's backup. -amm; the fit with 5.5.3.8 - akienasus_cc_0
